To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the communication traffic for blockchain synchronization of IoT devices is dominated by the number of accounts that are updated by the IoT device, and by the number of IoT devices connected to each validator node.
the communication traffic for blockchain synchronization is dominated by the size of blocks, and that it can be significantly reduced by using a gossip-based protocol.

the synchronization protocols that use the blockchain network for synchronization are more energy efficient than the ones that use a separate communication channel, and that the energy efficiency of these protocols increases with the number of devices and the size of the blocks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a novel synchronization scheme that is able to provide the IoT devices with the most recent blockchain information, while reducing the communication cost and power consumption.
, the blockchain technology is well suited for IoT devices in terms of communication traffic, power consumption, and security.
, we propose a new architecture and protocol that can be used to synchronize the IoT devices to a blockchain, while minimizing the communication traffic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synchronization protocols that rely on wireless communications can be more energy efficient than the protocols that use wired connections.

the synchronization traffic can be reduced by a factor of 10,000 with respect to the naive solution, and that the synchronization traffic scales with the number of accounts and the number of transactions per second, but not with the number of devices.

a careful design of the blockchain synchronization protocol is needed to minimize the synchronization latency and the communication overhead, while preserving the privacy and security of the IoT devices.
